Codelists specifications

Source: vignettes/codelists-schema.Rmd
codelists-schema.Rmd

_codelists.yml defines the codelists used in a study. It is an optional file in the study directory. Load it with mighty_codelists(), either directly or as the @codelists property of mighty_study(). Columns refer to a codelist by its id in their codelist field. The file structure is defined by a JSON-schema accessible with:

system.file("schema", "codelists.json", package = "mighty.metadata")

Structure

The file is a list of codelists. Each codelist has the following fields:

Field Type Description
id string Unique id used to reference the codelist from column metadata (required)
label string Codelist label
description string Codelist description
datatype string Data type of the coded values: text, integer or float
values list Values of a sponsor-defined codelist
subset list Values to keep from an external codelist
restore list SDTM CT values to include even when not used in the SDTM define.xml
extend list Values extending an extensible external codelist

Entries in values and extend have a code and an optional decode (intended for TranslatedText in define.xml); entries in subset and restore have only a code. Each group must have at least one entry, and within a group either all or none of the entries have a decode.

Operation groups

Each codelist has an id and at least one of four operation groups. The groups fall into two kinds: a sponsor-defined codelist, or changes to a codelist from an external source of controlled terminology (e.g. CDISC CT).

Group Kind Entries Purpose
values Sponsor-defined code, optional decode Defines all values of a codelist that does not exist externally
subset External code Keeps only these values from the external codelist
restore External code Includes SDTM controlled terminology values in the ADaM codelist even when they are not used in the SDTM define.xml
extend External code, optional decode Adds sponsor-defined values to an extensible external codelist

A codelist with values must also have label, description and datatype. For the other groups these fields are optional, as they come from the external codelist.

values cannot be combined with subset or restore on the same codelist. Codelist ids must be unique, and code must be unique across all groups within a codelist (compared as text, so 1 and "1" are duplicates).

Example 

# A sponsor-defined codelist
- id: REGION
  label: Codelist for region
  description: Region codelist
  datatype: text
  values:
    - code: EUROPE
      decode: Europe
    - code: NORTH AMERICA
      decode: North America

# Keep two values of an external codelist and restore one more
- id: AGEU
  subset:
    - code: YEARS
    - code: MONTHS
  restore:
    - code: DAYS

# Add a sponsor-defined value to an extensible external codelist
- id: LOC
  extend:
    - code: MY CUSTOM LOCATION
      decode: My Custom Location

A column refers to a codelist by its id:

columns:
  - id: REGION
    label: Region
    codelist: REGION

Codelists do not have to be referenced by a column, e.g. when they are added before the columns that use them. Use check_codelist_references() to check that every codelist in a study is referenced by at least one column (including columns within parameters). It does not check the opposite direction: a column referring to a codelist that is not defined in _codelists.yml is not reported.

code can be a string or a number. Since yaml infers types, unquoted values that look like numbers (e.g. code: 1) are read as numbers.
